subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Warcraft-style wolf model facing forward, with chunky exaggerated proportions, big paws, thick ruff, and bold painted fur, starting with a root hips joint for the skeleton structure.

Now I'm working out joint placements: a spine chain from hips through chest, a neck chain leading to the head and jaw, a tail chain curving backward with three segments, and front legs positioned with shoulders and paw targets for a sturdy stance.

Now I'm setting up the sweep chains for each leg, naming the shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw joints so the limb point arrays map to spans plus a tip segment, and double-checking which side convention (+X vs -X) corresponds to left versus right.

For attaching the legs and torso, I'm figuring out which spine joint index serves as the parent for front legs near the chest versus hind legs near the hips, then sketching how to loft the body as a sweep along the spine path with a radius function driving the cross-section.

Still defining body shape...

Adding a spiked fur ruff ring around the neck using outward-tilted spikes swept backward for a windblown look, placed at two points along the neck. Now I'm orienting the head joint forward from the neck tip, angling it slightly downward.

Building the skull as a scaled sphere, with a tapering muzzle frustum box in front, a dark nose tip, and a separate jaw joint below the skull aimed forward and down for the lower jaw frustum.

Adding fangs as white cones, a dark inner mouth box, and a slight jaw-open pose for realism before moving to the ears, which I'm extruding as sharp triangular outlines per side.

For eye placement I'm working out a local coordinate helper that takes forward/up/left offsets relative to the head, trusting signed values to mirror correctly between left and right sides, then planning an amber wolf-eye decal via SVG.

I'll add a small brow ridge of dark fur angled over the eye, and consider glowing the eye decal amber for that fierce look. For the eye texture itself, I'm sketching an almond-shaped SVG with amber fill, dark outline, a slit pupil, and a highlight, mirrored for the opposite side. Then I'll move on to the paws, built from scaled spheres with small clawed toes at the tips.

Still writing claw and leg geometry...

Now I'm working out the tail as a tapering sweep chain, bushy near the base and narrowing to a point at the tip, and starting to define the fur paint function with a base coat color.

Still writing coat paint logic...

Lighter legs below a threshold, darkening the tail tip near its end point. I'm noting the SDK imports needed (builder, rng, catmull curves, limb, paint, noise, mix, smoothstep, glow kit) and thinking through Warcraft-style wolf details like pauldron-like shoulder fur, a scarred ear, a facial battle scar, and a studded leather collar.

Adding spiky dorsal mane...

Adding a thin pink scar rod across the left eye, then setting up a neck fur ring along the neck chain's tangent frame with spikes leaning back slightly, varying colors per item for a natural coat look. Now moving on to the chest ruff.

For the chest I'm placing a light cream fur bib using a scaled sphere on the lower front, then adding a partial spike ring across its lower arc for texture, anchored to the nearest bone joint. I'm also making sure the neck chain correctly parents off the end of the spine path so the body sweep and neck segment connect smoothly.

Now I'm reworking the spine and neck point coordinates so the body extends further forward before the neck rises up to a raised, alert head position, and naming each joint segment (spine1-3, neck1-3) for the bone roles.

The head joint should parent to the last neck joint using the tip reference. For the tail, I'm laying out four points from the hips backward, yielding three spans named tail1 through tail4, and I'm working out how the body sweep bone list should include both the hips joint and the spine chain so the sweep path starts correctly at the hips.

For the body shape, I'm extending the path further back to cover the hindquarters, adding a straight extension at the start cap and relying on haunch spheres to cover the hind leg hip area. I'm also defining a radius profile that widens toward the chest with a slight downward shift for depth.

Checking the resulting body height against a wolf's proportions, I realize the current shift and radius values push the back too tall compared to the head -- around 1.09 versus a target of roughly 0.95 -- so I need to lower the spine height to keep things stylized but proportionate.

Let me rework the spine coordinates and joint positions: hips, mid-spine, and chest get adjusted y-values with tighter radii, bringing the chest top to about 0.96 and bottom near 0.52, with hips topping around 0.85. I'm also setting the shoulder joint height, the neck curve rising toward the head, and confirming the overall silhouette height (ears reaching roughly 1.3) fits a bold, Warcraft-style stylization, then placing the hip and hind leg joint coordinates accordingly.

Now I'm working out the front leg geometry—shoulder and target positions, segment lengths, and bend directions so the limb reaches naturally with a slight bow at the elbow and wrist. I'm confirming that with three or more segments, the solver keeps the final segment aligned with the bend hint, then moving on to set up chain sweeps with varying radius profiles for the legs, starting with the hind limb's joint names.

Adding more head parts...

Still working out eye decal geometry...

Shaping the ear outline...

The slight poke-through is fine since it's centered either way. Skipping the ear tuft fur, I'm adding cheek ruff spikes as a looped set of light-grey cones per side, then placing upper fang cones on the head pointing downward in ivory.

Now I'm positioning lower fangs on the jaw pointing upward, shaping the jaw with a frustum box tapering toward the chin in a lighter coat color, and adding a dark interior box between the jaws to suggest the mouth cavity.

Next I'm defining the jaw joint between head and jaw bone, aiming it forward, then applying a slight 8-degree downward pose to leave the mouth open. After that I'm placing shoulder spheres scaled and positioned near the spine joint, followed by haunch spheres on the opposite end.

Continuing color placement based on world position for continuity, then adding a dorsal mane swept along the body with spikes angled back and up, varying length sinusoidally and colored dark gray, plus ruff rings and a swept, painted tail. I'm also adding paws, claws, and shoulder fur tufts as spikes based at the elbow joint position.

Now I'm positioning additional spikes at the hock joint for the hind legs, and making sure paw bottoms and claws sit correctly on the ground plane. The eyes get a glow decal, and I'm finalizing the part count around 150, which feels efficient though a bit under target, so I'm considering a few extra details like chest bib spikes or a scarred ear, and ultimately deciding to add a small glowing frost rune marking on the shoulder for visual interest.

Writing the shoulder rune decal...

Now I'm settling on a random function for spike variation and sketching the catmull path for the body, with bones mapped to spine and hips for the sweep geometry.

Next I'm working out the tail path with its own parent bone and tapering radii down to zero at the tip, plus a thicker neck chain with its own radius taper.

I'm also setting up the paint function signature returning an Rgb value, then writing the coat shader logic that mixes grey and tan based on smoothstep noise thresholds.

Writing coat shader...

Still refining shading logic...
